// diagnostic E0140

Jet.SingleUseDropped

`#SingleUse` value dropped without being consumed at scope end

What

`#SingleUse` value dropped without being consumed at scope end

Why

A `#SingleUse` value carries a job that must be done, so dropping it leaves that job undone

Fix

Consume the `#SingleUse` value before scope end.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.SingleUseDropped: Tests/UI/BrowserBidi/native_bidi_session_handles_cannot_cross_tasks_or_channels.stderr.

Error: Jet.ValueNotSendable: `session` can't cross into a task because `browser.Browser` isn't sendable
  --> Tests/UI/BrowserBidi/native_bidi_session_handles_cannot_cross_tasks_or_channels.jet:10:26
    |
 10 |     handle: task session.close()
    |                          ^^^^^
 Why: `Browser` is declared `#Local`, so its values stay on the thread that made them; tasks and channels move owned values between threads
 Fix: Give the task plain owned data, or rebuild the value as an owned copy before spawning
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.ValueNotSendable

Error: Jet.ValueNotSendable: `session` can't be sent because `browser.Browser` isn't sendable
  --> Tests/UI/BrowserBidi/native_bidi_session_handles_cannot_cross_tasks_or_channels.jet:12:17
    |
 12 |     sender.send(session)
    |                 ^^^^^^^
 Why: `Browser` is declared `#Local`, so its values stay on the thread that made them; tasks and channels move owned values between threads
 Fix: Send plain owned data instead, or rebuild the value as an owned copy before calling `.send()`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.ValueNotSendable

Error: Jet.SingleUseDropped: `handle` still owes `join` or `detach`
  --> Tests/UI/BrowserBidi/native_bidi_session_handles_cannot_cross_tasks_or_channels.jet:10:5
    |
 10 |     handle: task session.close()
    |     ^^^^^^
 Why: This value's type is `#SingleUse`, so it carries a job that has to be done — dropping it without doing that job leaves the work undone (an unjoined task, an unreleased lock)
 Fix: Consume it exactly once: call `.join()` or `.detach()` on it, pass it to a `^^` parameter, or `return` it — or write `#Unsafe("reason") { consume(handle) }` to discard it deliberately
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.SingleUseDropped
